normal_signature: First-person perspective from inside a vehicle looking forward
Vehicle dashboard or hood visible in the immediate foreground
Road surface extending into the distance with lane markings
Surrounding environment includes parked or moving vehicles
Street infrastructure such as trees, buildings, or signs visible
Treat bright, geometric light reflections or glare on the road surface as normal environmental artifacts, not defects.
Treat standard night highway traffic with visible brake lights and lane markings as normal, even if scene brightness is low.
Do not flag low-contrast, elongated road surface reflections or shadows as pedestrians unless distinct human features are clearly visible.
Do not classify standard highway infrastructure, such as concrete barriers or retaining walls, as road debris or anomalies.
Treat standard daytime urban traffic scenes with visible buses, cars, and city infrastructure as normal, even if agent uncertainty is moderate.
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Camera obstruction or failure resulting in a completely black, white, or static-filled image
Perspective shift where the camera is not mounted on a vehicle (e.g., aerial view, pedestrian view)
Absence of a drivable road surface (e.g., view of a wall, sky, or interior room)
Severe motion blur or distortion indicating sensor malfunction rather than vehicle speed
Classify as anomaly if the scene depicts a rural setting (e.g., cornfields) instead of the expected urban street environment.
Classify any traffic cone or temporary obstruction placed directly on tram tracks as an anomaly.
Flag images containing vintage vehicles or recreational trailers as anomalies, as the baseline class strictly contains modern traffic scenes.
Classify as anomaly if the scene depicts a rural setting with a vehicle towing a trailer, deviating from the standard urban street baseline.
Classify any wild animal detected on the road surface as a definitive anomaly, regardless of its posture or apparent calmness.
rules: if the image shows a dashboard, hood, or windshield wipers in the foreground then lean normal
if the image shows a road surface extending away from the camera then lean normal
if the image is completely black, white, or filled with digital noise then lean anomaly
if the image shows a view from a pedestrian height or aerial view without vehicle parts then lean anomaly
if the image shows a static indoor scene or a solid wall without a road then lean anomaly
